mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: The image in a convex side-view mirror is smaller than the actual vehicle.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when The image in a convex side-view mirror is smaller than the actual vehicle is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: A convex mirror forms erect, smaller images and gives a larger view area than a plane mirror, so it helps show more of the surroundings behind or around the observer. outward curvature leads to smaller erect images and a wider view area The learner explains that convex mirrors are used because they give erect smaller images and a larger view area. A side-view mirror should show vehicles at their actual size, so a plane mirror must be the safest choice.
